papers.abstract: Quantum machine learning offers new approaches to multivariate event classification in high-energy physics, but its performance relative to optimized classical methods remains uncertain under limited training data and restricted quantum resources. We investigate the sample-size scalability and representation sensitivity of a quantum support vector machine and a variational quantum classifier for Higgs-boson signal--background discrimination using simulated events from the ATLAS Higgs Machine Learning Challenge. The models are trained on balanced subsets ranging from 250 to 4000 events and evaluated on held-out samples preserving the original class distribution. Principal component analysis (PCA) and autoencoder (AE) representations are examined to reduce the input dimensionality and quantum-resource requirements. Four optimized classical classifiers are used as benchmarks under a common preprocessing, validation, and evaluation protocol. We assess training-sample scalability in classical and quantum classifiers using a four-component PCA representation and examine representation sensitivity through a secondary matched-event comparison of four- and eight-component PCA representations. Within the evaluated Higgs-boson classification setting, the QSVM showed stronger performance than the VQC at larger training sample sizes, while remaining below the best-performing classical classifiers.

papers.title: Active Neural Matter: A Finite-Window Response Framework for Physical Systems and Distributed AI Workflows
papers.abstract: Physical systems and distributed AI workflows can retain past information, receive delayed feedback and combine conflicting signals. These features pose a common modeling problem: determining what information about past interactions a state must retain to account for future responses. Active Neural Matter (ANM) addresses this problem through a finite-window response framework. Forward analysis uses each system's dynamics to predict state and output responses to perturbations, separating propagation from output sensitivity. Inverse analysis tests whether a candidate state retains enough information for these responses. With the system and future inputs or interaction rules fixed, distinguishable responses from histories assigned the same state identify distinctions the representation must preserve. Their distributional separation gives a lower bound on the worst-case error of approximating behavior from that state. Uncertainty bounds distinguish rejection, support within a fixed tolerance on tested comparisons, and unresolved cases. Delayed-consensus simulations check analytical predictions of response amplitude and phase over a narrow range of delays; flocking illustrates dependence on the chosen observable. An exact delayed-return construction establishes a sufficient state for a specified program. The AI studies identify distinctions in interaction history and evidence order that a representation must preserve to reproduce observed response distributions. Tests on new histories in a controlled feedback task provide bounded support for a state specified by the task instructions; the instructed rule predicts every observed action. ANM connects response prediction to measurable information requirements, separating behavioral fidelity from task correctness and initial-state adequacy from a closed evolution law for that state.

papers.title: Entanglement-Capability-Aware Finite-Bond Circuit Cutting for Distributed Quantum Computing
papers.abstract: Distributed quantum computing distributes workloads that exceed a single processor's capacity across resource-constrained components. Circuit cutting enables this decomposition, but its effectiveness depends on partition choice. We present SACE, a Simulation-Aware Circuit Partitioning framework with Entanglement-Capability-Aware Screening. EP-Cost screens partitions using a parameter-dependent entanglement-capability proxy and native implementation cost. Under reconstruction constraints, finite-bond refinement selects the candidate that minimizes the worst-subcircuit discrepancy between normalized MPS simulations at bond dimensions $\chi$ and $2\chi$. Across 14 exhaustively enumerated small-scale candidate spaces, EP-Cost-guided genetic algorithm selections attain co-optimal native quasiprobability decomposition (QPD) overhead, with a median within-circuit Spearman correlation of 0.9965 between EP-Cost and QPD overhead. At matched cut counts, EP-Cost reduces QPD overhead by $25.20\times$ and $16.89\times$ for 8- and 9-qubit QFT circuits, respectively, and improves sampled reconstruction. On 12-qubit approximate QFT, deterministic reconstruction reduces Pauli-observable mean absolute error in all six low-bond conditions and total-variation distance in five. With five cuts and 7,776 QPD terms, SACE is best on all four reconstruction metrics in four of six conditions. At 24 qubits, SACE improves exact-local QFT accuracy in all 30 instance-bond-dimension conditions against each EP-Cost-only, Kernighan-Lin, and spectral baseline. The 50-qubit QFT comparisons remain favorable as reference convergence improves. Weighted QAOA circuits provide complementary, more bond-sensitive evidence. Refinement benefits persist across three search methods; larger candidate panels improve the optimized proxy without guaranteeing lower exact-local error.
authors: Weidong Liu, Qingqing Jiang, Yufu Liu, Ruiqing He, Jiandong Shang, Hengliang Guo, Qiang Chen

papers.title: Exploring Dynamical Quantum Phase Transitions via the Dynamical Phase Accumulated at an Equilibrium Critical Point
papers.abstract: We investigate dynamical quantum phase transitions (DQPTs) generated by a two-step linear quench with a finite waiting time at the equilibrium critical point. The waiting stage leads to the accumulation of a dynamical phase that depends on the waiting time and directly reflects the critical spectral structure. In the transverse Ising chain, this accumulated phase modifies the critical structure of DQPTs from a single-critical-mode (SCM) regime to a multiple-critical-mode (MCM) regime. We analytically and numerically determine the boundary between the two regimes. Along this boundary, the waiting time approaches a constant in the sudden-quench limit, whereas in the slow-quench limit it follows Kibble--Zurek (KZ) scaling with the quench time. In the SCM regime, the rate function exhibits a conventional linear singularity, $r(t)-r(t^{*})\propto |t-t^{*}|^\alpha$, with the critical exponent $\alpha=1$ near the critical time. At the SCM--MCM boundary, this exponent changes to $\alpha=1/2$, leading to a divergent first derivative of the rate function. Additional discrete parameter lines with $\alpha=1/2$ also appear within the MCM regime in the parameter plane spanned by the waiting and quench times. Our findings establish a direct connection between the accumulated dynamical phase and the critical structure of DQPTs, further supported by an extended Su--Schrieffer--Heeger (SSH) model.
authors: Han-Chuan Kou, Peng Li, Zhi-Han Zhang, Zhen-Yu Zheng

papers.title: Scalability and performance metrics for boson sampling devices
papers.abstract: Linear-optical platforms provide a promising route to demonstrate quantum computational advantage, particularly through the boson sampling problem. While a boson sampling system should be large enough to show the quantum advantage, the size of the boson sampling problem is often restricted by experimental constraints. In particular, as a boson sampling system is scaled up, experimental constraints can limit its effective problem size to permit efficient classical simulation. In this paper, we investigate the theoretical scalability bounds for boson sampling systems under practical experimental conditions, including photon loss, mode mismatch, and input state error. We employ non-negativity conditions for phase-space quasiprobability distribution functions to analyze these effects. In addition, we introduce two device-level metrics, the boson sampling score which measures the usable capacity of a given device and the boson sampling volume which provides a common hardware-level benchmark for comparing different platforms and assessing their access to an advantage-relevant problem size regime. Our results provide fundamental insights into the performance of boson sampling systems under realistic experimental conditions and offer practical guidelines for scaling up boson sampling systems.
authors: Dong-Gil Im, Chung-Hyun Lee, Joonsuk Huh, Yoon-Ho Kim

papers.title: Cetraro lectures on integrable systems and moduli spaces of curves
papers.abstract: In these lecture notes we review some constructions and results on the relation between topology of the moduli space of stable curves and integrable systems of evolutionary PDEs.

papers.title: Reducing Trust Cost in Quantum Application Development Using AI
papers.abstract: Generative AI can be a powerful tool for supporting the design and implementation of quantum applications, whereas the burden of checking whether generated circuits realize the intended computation increases. In this study, we regard this burden of human understanding, checking, and judgment as ``trust cost,'' and propose a development methodology that integrates AI and formal verification to reduce it. In the proposed development methodology, the implementation is divided into three components: a target mathematical specification, a quantum circuit, and a correspondence theorem and its proof that prove the agreement between the two. This division separates the specifications and theorem statements checked by humans from the theorem proofs entrusted to mechanical checking. As a concrete development example of this proposal, we describe an implementation for the time evolution of a stochastic particle system and its results.

papers.title: A critical coupling for the magnetic instability of holographic SU(2) plasmas
papers.abstract: We show that gravity can remove the linear magnetic instability of a holographic plasma with an $SU(2)$ global symmetry. In the probe limit, charged vector bosons become tachyonic in their lowest Landau level above a critical field and condense into a vortex lattice. In Einstein-$SU(2)$ Yang-Mills theory in AdS$_5$ we include the backreaction of the field exactly, expanding only in the condensate around the D'Hoker-Kraus magnetic brane. The critical field diverges as the coupling $\alpha = \kappa^2/\hat g^2$ approaches $\alpha_\star = 2/3$, above which the normal phase has no linear charged instability at any field or temperature: we show this at zero temperature and establish it numerically at finite temperature. At zero temperature the field cancels from the mass of the lowest Landau level in the brane's AdS$_3 \times \mathbb{R}^2$ throat, and the instability is a violation of the throat's Breitenlohner-Freedman bound. The onset temperature vanishes at $\alpha_\star$ with an essential singularity of Berezinskii-Kosterlitz-Thouless type. For two-derivative Einstein-Yang-Mills duals in $d = 4$, 5 and 6 dimensions the normal phase has a charged instability if and only if $C_J/C_T < 8/(d^2(d+1))$, one tenth in $d = 4$. Above $\alpha_L = 0.372$ the gravitational attraction between vortices makes the uniform lattice unstable and the transition first order, so $B_c$ is only a spinodal; whether a condensed phase survives above $\alpha_\star$ is left open.

papers.title: Clifford Invariants and Three-Copy Quantum Tests
papers.abstract: We give an explicit treatment of the third tensor power of the Clifford representation on $n$ qutrits, for $n\geq2$. This representation has five pairwise inequivalent irreducible constituents, with multiplicities $1,1,1,1,2$. The decomposition reduces the Clifford twirl of a tensor cube to four real parameters. Two of them are spectral moments of the input. The other two are cubic invariants expressed as sums of cubes of the Weyl characteristic function and the discrete Wigner function. On trace-one Hermitian matrices, the invariant polynomials of degree at most three are spanned by the constant function and four algebraically independent functions. These functions do not separate Clifford orbits. For pure inputs a single parameter suffices. We recover its range and the characterization of its maximum by stabilizer states. We bound the stabilizer fidelity, determine full separability across the three copies in the symmetric family, and recover the criterion for a complex projective $3$-design. We classify the jointly invariant quantum Boolean functions. For stabilizer testing and for testing unknown observables we give explicit bounds on copies and queries. We also give character formulas for the finite projective Clifford groups and record the complete character table for two qutrits.

papers.title: Avoiding Defects within Heavy-Hexagon Architecture
papers.abstract: When implementing scalable fault-tolerant quantum computing using superconducting quantum processors, one of the critical challenges to overcome is the presence of defective qubits arising from fabrication and calibration imperfections. A defect on a specific qubit severely restricts the connectivity between adjacent qubits, disrupts stabilizer measurements, induces frequent detection events, and consequently inflates the logical error rate. To mitigate this issue, various strategies have been proposed, such as syndrome extraction circuits based on stabilizer folding and the construction of super-stabilizers via gauge operators. However, these methods have primarily been developed for architectures with relatively high connectivity of 3 to 4. Furthermore, experimental demonstrations showing an actual reduction in logical error rates in the presence of physical hardware defects have been lacking. In this work, we propose a defect-avoidance scheme tailored for the heavy-hexagon architecture, which features a lower connectivity of 2 to 3. While previous approaches required four measurement cycles to measure all gauge operators comprising a super-stabilizer, our proposed scheme completes all gauge measurements within only two cycles. We experimentally validate this approach on IBM quantum hardware by identifying physical defects and implementing the defect-avoidance circuits. As a result, avoiding the defect yields an approximately 10\% reduction in the logical error rate per cycle for both logical $X$ and $Z$ errors. These findings demonstrate that defects in superconducting hardware can be successfully handled even under the constrained connectivity of heavy-hexagon lattices, and that defect avoidance substantially reduces logical errors on real quantum hardware.

papers.title: Classical Communication Helps Single-Shot Quantum Compression
papers.abstract: Free classical communication can yield an unbounded single-shot saving in quantum compression, even though it leaves the asymptotic rate of an i.i.d. source unchanged. At every fixed error in $(0,1)$, we exhibit sources whose unassisted compression cost is arbitrarily large, yet a single qubit suffices with classical communication and no preshared entanglement. We establish this separation by determining the exact optimal source fidelity for compression through an $m$-dimensional noiseless quantum channel, with and without free classical communication, while preserving correlations with an inaccessible reference. Without classical assistance, the optimal fidelity is exactly the Ky Fan norm $\|\rho\|_{(m)}$, the sum of the $m$ largest eigenvalues of the source state. With classical assistance, we obtain an explicit spectral threshold formula and a protocol attaining it. Classical communication strictly improves fidelity whenever $m$ is smaller than the source rank. The corresponding compression costs are two smoothed versions of the log-rank entropy, also called max-entropy: trace-distance smoothing under local operations and quadratic smoothing under LOCC. For i.i.d. copies of a fixed source with positive entropy variance, however, the two costs have identical first-, second-, and third-order asymptotic terms. For nonlattice spectra, we determine the constant-order advantage: classical communication saves $\log_2(e)-1$ bits per block asymptotically, and the ratio of assisted to unassisted minimum communication dimensions converges to $2/e$.

papers.title: Global Well-Posedness and Uniform Long-Time Control for a Class of Periodic NLS-Dysthe Equations
papers.abstract:
We study a class of periodic NLS-Dysthe (NLS-Dy) equations, also referred to as higher-order nonlinear Schr"odinger equations (HNLS), of the form $i\partial_t u+a\partial_x^2u+b|u|^2u+i\varepsilon(c\partial_x^3u+d|u|^2\partial_xu+eu^2\partial_x\overline{u})=0$ with $ x\in\mathbb T$, $a,b,c,d,e\in\mathbb R$, $abc
eq0$, and $\varepsilon>0$. For $0<\varepsilon\ll1$, equations of this type arise as higher-order modulation models for some nonlinear dispersive PDEs, including the Klein-Gordon equation and the Serre-Green-Naghdi equation modeling the evolution of nonlinear shallow water waves. We prove local well-posedness in $H^s(\mathbb T)$ for $s>3/2$ for arbitrary admissible coefficients, and establish an $H^1$ continuation criterion for $s\ge2$. In the parameter regime $e
eq0$, a lower-order conservation law provides uniform $H^1$ control and, together with the continuation criterion, yields global well-posedness for $s\ge2$. This result does not require the non-resonance condition appearing in Takaoka's periodic theory, while the condition $e
eq0$ naturally arises in the modulation setting considered here. Finally, motivated by the long-time regime relevant for modulation, we establish uniform long-time control without imposing a smallness assumption on the initial datum. Using the conservation laws of cubic NLS and their invariance under the commuting complex mKdV flow, we obtain uniform $H^s$ bounds on time intervals of order $\varepsilon^{-1}$ for integer $s\ge2$. For non-integer real $s\ge2$, the maximal $H^s$ solution exists on the same time scale, while uniform control is obtained at a lower regularity, with a loss of less than one derivative.

papers.title: Entanglement generation from degeneracy breaking of superradiant Liouvillian steady states by local operations
papers.abstract: Superradiance is a collective optical effect where emitters cooperatively radiate with a maximal intensity scaling proportional to the square of the number of emitters. Despite the superradiant cascade transitioning through highly entangled states, it has been shown that, for dynamics along the Dicke ladder, superradiance need not generate entanglement between the emitters. By contrast, we show how introducing incoherent local processes -- normally considered detrimental to both entanglement and superradiance -- can generate high levels of inter-emitter entanglement. We develop a general framework, using degenerate non-Hermitian perturbation theory, for the study of superradiant Liouvillian steady-state degeneracy breaking by these local operations from a few emitters up into the thermodynamic limit. From this, we are able to show that entanglement becomes ubiquitous in this regime and demonstrate its robustness against other forms of symmetric environmental noise. In the regime where pumping dominates, we find that population accumulates towards the maximally entangled minimal pseudo-spin states, corresponding to multi-emitter singlet states. This provides a deeper insight into many-body entanglement and the curious connection between local operations and entanglement generation.

papers.title: On best approximation and estimates of Bohr--Favard type on the sphere for functions with bounded Laplacian
papers.abstract: We determine the best constants in estimates of the $L^\infty$ norm of functions on the sphere with bounded Laplacian whose first spherical harmonic components vanish. In every dimension $d\geq2$, these constants are expressed through weighted $L^1$ extremal polynomials. On $S^2$ the constant is an explicit positive series, and the best coefficient of $n^{-2}$ is $7\zeta(3)/4$. On $S^3$ the best coefficient of $n^{-2}$ is a positive integral involving the H\"ormander--Bernhardsson extremal function. In higher dimensions the rescaled extremal polynomials converge to weighted entire extremals, which give asymptotic formulas for the Bohr constants on $S^4$ and $S^6$. The most unexpected and, in our view, interesting observation is that, for every fixed $n\geq2$ on $S^2$ and $S^3$, the constants in best approximation estimates are \emph{strictly smaller} than the corresponding Bohr--Favard constants.

papers.title: Lifts of symmetries to minimal nondegenerate extensions are unique up to fermion attachment
papers.abstract: Gauging fermion parity in a $(2+1)$-dimensional fermionic topological order requires lifting its symmetries to the resulting bosonic theory. We give a direct tensor-categorical proof that, for a slightly degenerate braided fusion category $\mathcal{C}$ and a fixed minimal nondegenerate extension ${\cal E}$, the restriction homomorphism $r\colon\operatorname{Aut}_{\mathrm{LR}}(\mathcal{E})\to \operatorname{Aut}_{\mathrm{LR}}(\mathcal{C})$ on classes of complex-linear locality-respecting (LR) braided autoequivalences is surjective with central kernel $\mathbb{Z}/2$, generated by fermion attachment. Thus each symmetry class has exactly two LR lift classes, related by attaching the fermion to every vortex. We apply graded Morita theory to reduce the kernel to two module types on the vortex sector, corresponding to tensoring with the vacuum or the fermion. We then prove relative rigidity to show that each type determines a unique LR class, which are distinguished by fermionic self-braiding even when their actions on simple-object labels coincide. We prove surjectivity by extending graph algebras in $\mathcal{C}^{\mathrm{rev}}\boxtimes\mathcal{C}$ to Lagrangian algebras in $\mathcal{E}^{\mathrm{rev}}\boxtimes\mathcal{E}$. Our results require neither unitarity nor a ribbon structure. We illustrate the lifting ambiguity in the Laughlin state, the $SO(3)_3$ theory and the Ising topological order.

papers.title: Overlap distributions under the Gibbs measure of a Haar model of $\log|\zeta|$ on and near the critical line
papers.abstract: We study the Gibbs measure of $H(h) = \Re\sum_{p^{j} \leq X}U_{p}^{j}/(j p^{j(\sigma + i h)})$, a random field modeling large values of the log-modulus of the Riemann zeta function on and near the critical line, where the $U_{p}$ are independent and uniformly distributed on the complex unit circle. Writing $t = \log \log T$, the cutoff $X$ and real part $\sigma$ may vary with $T$ subject to $T^{1/t^{\Phi}} \leq X \leq T^{1/t^{\phi}}$ and $0 \leq \sigma - 1/2 \leq C_{\sigma}t^{\Phi}/\log T$, for fixed $\Phi \geq \phi > 1/2$ and $C_{\sigma} > 0$. On $I_{\theta} = [ - (\log T)^{\theta},(\log T)^{\theta}]$, define the Gibbs measure $G_{\beta,\sigma,T}^{\mathrm{H}}(\mathrm{d}h) := e^{\beta H(h)}\mathrm{d}h/\int_{I_{\theta}}e^{\beta H(h')}\mathrm{d}h'$. For every fixed $\theta > - 1$ and inverse temperature $\beta > 0$, the limiting joint distributions of correlations (overlaps) among points sampled from this measure are determined after averaging over the Haar phases. At and below $\beta_{c}(\theta) = 2\sqrt{1 + (\theta \vee 0)}$, the limiting two-overlap distribution is concentrated at $q_{0} = |\theta \wedge 0|$. Above this threshold, it assigns masses $\beta_{c}(\theta)/\beta$ and $1 - \beta_{c}(\theta)/\beta$ to $q_{0}$ and $1$, respectively, and the limiting joint overlap distribution is described by a Poisson-Dirichlet process of parameter $\beta_{c}(\theta)/\beta$. Approximate Ghirlanda-Guerra identities are shown to hold uniformly for bounded deterministic functions of the sampled positions. This paper is the first in a series devoted to extending these results to $\log|\zeta|$ near the critical line.

papers.title: Spiral Edge States in Topological 2D Sb2Te3 Crystals
papers.abstract: This work explores the edge state conduction properties of twinned and spiraled, 2D Sb2Te3 topological insulator crystals. We show the structure supports spatially continuous edge states within two spiral and knotted edge conduction channels. The channels are connected through a topological defect. This geometry introduces boundary conditions into the 2D crystal that modifies the edge state dispersion. Using a combination of low loss Electron Energy Loss Spectroscopy, Magnetic Force Microscopy and traditional carrier transport measurements we identify a distinct excitation at 0.155 eV in the spiral that seems to be related to two isolated states within the gap. This state is localized to the crystal edges. The modification of edge state bands using manipulation of a systems quantum geometry may open new avenues for the use of 2D topological systems.
authors: Timothy Carlson, Daniel Lazega, Scott McGuire, Mihirangi Medahinne, Motahhare Mirhosseini, Gabriel Marcus, ChaoChao Dun, Maria Kolesnik-Gray, Vojislav Krstic, David Carroll

papers.title: Quantum Energy Inequalities with a twist: rotating frames along stationary worldlines
papers.abstract: The energy densities of the quantised scalar and electromagnetic fields need not be positive, but their averages along timelike worldlines are constrained by Quantum Energy Inequalities (QEIs) that hold in flat and curved spacetimes for arbitrary Hadamard quantum field states. However the general QEI bound is not easy to compute in closed form. Here, we compute closed form expressions for the massless scalar and electromagnetic fields along stationary worldlines in Minkowski spacetime. These worldlines are solutions to the four-dimensional Frenet-Serret equations with constant curvature invariants and include inertial, uniformly linearly accelerated, and uniformly rotating worldlines as special cases. The QEI bound depends on a choice of tetrad along the worldline, and we compute it for any tetrad with constant angular velocity relative to the Frenet-Serret tetrad. Optimising over the angular velocity, we show that the tightest electromagnetic QEI bound occurs when the tetrad is invariant under Fermi-Walker tetrads. Surprisingly, the Fermi-Walker tetrad does not produce the tightest QEI bound for massless scalar fields, and we investigate the optimal bound both analytically and numerically. Our results and methodology significantly improve on those in [CJ Fewster & J Thompson, Class. Quantum Grav. 40 (2023) 175008], in which only Frenet-Serret tetrads were considered for massless scalar fields.
authors: Christopher J. Fewster, Daniel Lomax Ford

papers.title: Charged Deformation of a Hairy Black Brane: Perturbative Solution and Thermodynamics
papers.abstract: We study electrically charged black branes in four-dimensional Einstein-Maxwell-scalar theory with Maxwell coupling $Z(\phi)=e^{3\phi/\sqrt7}$, whose potential has an AdS$_4$ fixed point only in the infrared. For nonzero hair parameter $\alpha$ the scalar grows logarithmically at large radius and the geometry is not asymptotically AdS, so the holographic dictionary is a working assumption. With the scale-invariant multi-trace boundary condition of the neutral branes, giving conformal thermodynamics, we work to second order in the charge, obtaining the Maxwell field and susceptibility in closed form, plus the thermodynamics, condensate, incoherent conductivity and cumulant ratio $T^2\chi_4/\chi_2=6c(\alpha)<0$ for all $\alpha$ considered. Independent perturbative computations and first-law closed forms agree within $4\times10^{-6}$; nonlinear solutions reproduce second-order results to $1.2\times10^{-5}$ and $c$ to $6\times10^{-4}$. They are locally thermodynamically stable where constructed, and the pressure is analytic in $(\mu_Q/T)^2$ near zero density. No regular extremal horizon exists at finite scalar value, and $\rho/s<\sqrt{21}/(2\pi)$ exactly. The extremal limit is an AdS$_2\times\mathbb R^2$ throat where the scalar grows as $\ln\ln(1/u)$ in the AdS$_2$ radial coordinate $u$; the bound is saturated there, and extremal values are approached as powers of $1/\ln(\mu_Q/T)$. With a Dirichlet condition on the scalar source, the same solutions describe a non-conformal theory with scale $\Lambda$, whose charged branes exist only below $T_{\max}(\mu_Q)$, which falls from $0.194\Lambda$ at zero density to zero at $\mu_Q=0.506\Lambda$. This boundary is a diffusive instability where the charge susceptibility diverges at nonzero density, and the bulk viscosity violates Buchel's bound at all densities. Quasinormal modes with the normalizable large-radius condition reproduce its hydrodynamics.

papers.title: A complete classification of operator controllability for closed three-level quantum systems driven by a single control
papers.abstract: In this work, we study operator controllability of finite-dimensional closed quantum systems driven by a single coherent control. Two general Lie-algebraic results on controllability of such systems are proved. The first gives sufficient conditions under which controllability of the system is preserved when controlled energy-level shifts are added. The second gives a sufficient basis-element condition under which the dynamical Lie algebra contains $\mathfrak{su}(N)$ and the system is therefore operator controllable. These results, together with known controllability conditions, are applied to obtain a complete classification of operator controllability of all three-level quantum systems in terms of their free and interaction Hamiltonian matrix elements. This classification covers all combinations of energy-level and level-spacing degeneracies, two or three allowed transitions, as well as the presence or absence of controlled energy-level shifts, and gives necessary and sufficient conditions for operator controllability in each case.

papers.title: Partial-coherence weak measurement of polarization qubits with a temporal pointer: theory and experiment
papers.abstract: Weak measurement has proven useful for metrology, for probing quantum paradoxes, and for the direct measurement of quantum states. Weak measurements of polarization qubits with temporal pointers provide a direct route to weak-value characterization, including in regimes where the pointer is only partially coherent. We derive a closed-form expression for the post-selected temporal shift that interpolates between the incoherent and coherent (ideal) weak-measurement limits through a single parameter $\nu$, the pointer visibility. The expression is experimentally tested for a range of polarization states spanning three trajectories corresponding to rotations about the principal axes of the Poincar\'e sphere. Two of the trajectories provide parameter-free benchmarks, with the real part of the weak value following $\cos^2\theta$ and $1/2$. In contrast, the weak value along the third trajectory is sensitive to incoherence and is well described by the single-parameter partial-coherence model, from which a reduced pointer visibility is obtained. Time shifts are extracted from the smoothed derivative of the pulse leading edge with internal calibration, reaching few-picosecond precision on 10 ns optical pulses using commercial components. The same apparatus also gives qualitative access to the imaginary quadrature through the frequency centroid, showing that temporal weak measurements remain accessible and quantitative in partially coherent pulsed systems.

papers.title: DisCo Algebra: Why Disintegration and Combination Are Not Inverses
papers.abstract: We present DisCo algebra---a compositional framework for joint probability built from a symmetric cooperad (disintegration) and a symmetric operad (combination) on the bare family $\mathcal{P}_n=\mathrm{Prob}([0,1]^n)$. No probability integral transform, no external summary functions, no enrichment of objects with conditional kernels. The disintegration side uses block-wise joint CDFs as intrinsic, measure-determined 1D summaries, yielding a lossy compression. The combination side reads the same summaries and reconstructs via regular conditional measures, yielding a lossless embedding. We prove that combination followed by disintegration is the identity on admissible inputs, but disintegration followed by combination is not---the information loss is exactly the conditional KL divergence between the true conditional distribution and the conditionally independent product. This asymmetry reveals a hard limit on how much cross-block dependence can be captured by scalar block summaries.

papers.title: Entanglement detection in dynamical quantum systems
papers.abstract: Quantum science and engineering increasingly target the exploitation and control of large-scale dynamical systems. As system size grows, novel phenomena and quantum advantages emerge, but the resulting many-body dynamics become correspondingly harder to monitor and characterize. In particular, the underlying Hamiltonian often lacks symmetries, and the induced many-body dynamics quickly become hard to track. Focusing on one of the most important quantum features---entanglement---we demonstrate that, for a broad class of common Hamiltonian models, one can design effective witnesses that detect both the presence and structure of entanglement over relatively long evolution times. Inspired by stabilizer-based simulation, we track the evolution of generalized stabilizers of the underlying state and use them to construct linear entanglement witnesses. Through numerical experiments on Heisenberg-type Hamiltonians with up to twelve qubits, we show that the required number of measurement settings can be kept at a modest scale as the system size increases, and entanglement detection remains effective over evolution times that significantly exceed those accessible to naive approaches. The corresponding calculations can be carried out largely symbolically. Furthermore, unlike accurate state simulation, the stabilizer-based design of entanglement witnesses can be performed in a much more coarse-grained, digitized manner. We hope these results will stimulate further exploration of the quantum control of large systems.
authors: Xingjian Zhang, Jiayi Wu, Jue Xu, Qi Zhao

papers.title: Generative learning of time series with holographic quantum circuit sampling
papers.abstract: Quantum generative models face growing qubit requirements and concentrated loss landscapes when learning long time series. Here we introduce holographic quantum circuit sampling (HQCS), which combines mid-circuit measurements, qubit reuse and independently parameterized temporal blocks to generate trajectories with a fixed number of qubits. For Haar-random HQCS and a normalized exponential kernel, we prove inverse-polynomial bounds on maximum mean discrepancy loss variance, contrasting with exponential concentration in global Haar-random generators. For generic members of a family of nonstationary Markov processes, temporal parameterization reduces exact-generation gate counts from quadratic to linear in sequence length relative to a specified class of repeated shared-block generators. Simulations demonstrate learning of Gaussian autoregressive processes and historical Volatility Index (VIX) trajectories, with the latter achieving over tenfold lower maximum mean discrepancy than the tested classical benchmarks. These results establish a framework for quantum time-series generation with fixed qubit requirements and provable avoidance of exponential loss concentration as sequence length grows.
authors: Bingzhi Zhang, Matthew W. Lee, Tom Finke, Quntao Zhuang

papers.title: Generative Quantum Machine Learning Methods for Cancer Detection using Augmented Datasets
papers.abstract: Cancer detection using AI methods and image databases faces several challenges, including limited and imbalanced image datasets, long algorithm training times, and high-complexity feature generation. In particular, many cancer image datasets contain very few malignant examples compared to benign ones, limiting the amount of minority-class data available for training. Although classical AI and especially deep learning methods have had some success in providing cancer diagnostics, Quantum Machine Learning (QML) methods may offer advantages through high-dimensional feature representations, generative data augmentation, and the exploitation of feature correlations through quantum properties such as entanglement. In this paper, we propose using a generative QML method on the compressed breast ultrasound image dataset (BUSI) to generate synthetic images and hence augmented datasets for classifier training. In particular, we train a convolutional neural network with real, synthetic, and a combination of real and synthetic images. We test the algorithm on real images and provide comparative results for all three training cases. Our results show that the classifier trained entirely on synthetic images achieved an AUC-ROC of 0.802 (80.2%), compared with 0.760 (76.0%) for the real-data baseline.
authors: Sophia Knutson, Nandika Goyal, Gennaro De Luca, Glen Uehara, Tanay Kamlesh Patel, Andreas Spanias

papers.title: Plane wave representation for wave scattering on a sphere
papers.abstract: Motivated by three-dimensional wave diffraction by conical shapes, we consider the two-dimensional problem of wave scattering on the real sphere $\mathcal{S}^2$ resulting from a point-source incidence on a scatterer $\mathbb{S}$. Using the recently introduced notion of plane waves on $\mathcal{S}^2$ as well as recent results on the Laplace--Beltrami Green's function $G$ on $\mathcal{S}^2$, we derive three plane-wave representations for the scattered field $u$. We then explain how $u$ can be analytically continued to the complexified sphere $\mathcal{S}^2_{\mathbb{c}}$. This allows us to formulate a complexified version of Green's third identity, and to provide a characterisation of complex sources. All our results are then used to draw strong analogies between planar and spherical scattering problems, notably through the introduction of directivities.
authors: Valentin D. Kunz, Andrey V. Shanin, Raphael C. Assier

papers.title: The R\'enyi area law conjecture is false below $\alpha=1$ in high dimensions
papers.abstract: Area laws express the expectation that entanglement in gapped quantum ground states scales with a boundary rather than a volume. In one dimension this holds for every R\'enyi entropy, and the R\'enyi area-law conjecture asserts the same in higher dimensions for each fixed $0<\alpha<1$. Here we disprove this conjecture in every spatial dimension two and higher. We construct finite-range Hamiltonians with fixed local dimension, bounded interaction strength, unique ground states and a uniform spectral gap, whose ground states exhibit volume-law R\'enyi entanglement while obeying a von Neumann area law and remaining connected to product states through uniformly gapped local paths. The mechanism is error-space complexity: locally identifiable components of arbitrarily small weight can encode states with high entanglement complexity. We also establish the worst-case rank-error trade-off for approximate ground-state projectors, a key tool in one-dimensional area-law proofs. At fixed gap, the optimal Schmidt rank at projection error $\epsilon$ across a planar cut of cross-section $A$ scales as $\exp[\tilde{\Theta}((A\log\epsilon^{-1})^{2/3})]$ when $\log\epsilon^{-1}\gtrsim A$. Thus $\alpha=1$ is the sharp threshold for a universal R\'enyi area law within this adiabatically connected class.

papers.title: Cosmology & Astrophysics of the Dark Dimension with Bulk Majorana Neutrinos
papers.abstract: Recently, the possibility of having sterile Majorana neutrinos charged under $B-L$ gauge symmetry in the bulk of the dark dimension has been explored. We point out a cosmological restriction on the Majorana mass of bulk neutrinos leading to mass $\gtrsim 100~{\rm GeV}$. This avoids the over-production of Kaluza-Klein neutrino towers in the early universe thus resolving the cosmological neutrino catastrophe of extra dimension scenarios. If the mass of the bulk neutrino is at the lower end of this bound, it can potentially also explain the recently observed Fermi halo excess on gamma rays through the evaporation of long-lived 5d (i.e. dark) black holes through Hawking radiation to bulk neutrinos, which promptly decay into standard model particles.

papers.title: Signal-to-noise problems in fault-tolerant quantum computation
papers.abstract: Quantum computation offers a promising alternative to classical Monte Carlo methods by naturally avoiding sign problems through unitary evolution. A common misconception follows from this: because quantum simulation sidesteps the sign problem, it is often assumed to be an essentially perfect substitute for classical sampling. This is false---quantum measurements are intrinsically stochastic, and estimating observables often requires a number of samples that grows exponentially with system size, time separation, or inverse temperature, exactly as in the classical signal-to-noise problem. In this work, we analyze the origin and structure of signal-to-noise problems in quantum computation, drawing parallels with classical Monte Carlo, and demonstrate that such noise persists even in sign-problem-free regimes. We discuss strategies to mitigate it, in particular a quantum generalization of Stein control variates construction, in which unbiased estimators are built from operator commutators $[X,A]$ and their discrete diagonal counterparts, and validate the approach with exactly solvable numerical examples that quantify the achievable variance reduction. Our results underscore that variance reduction, not merely sign-problem avoidance, is required to make quantum algorithms practically viable for many-body physics.

papers.title: Non-Intrusive Balancing for Data-Driven Model Reduction with Oblique Projections
papers.abstract: Non-intrusive reduced-order modeling is essential for systems simulated with black- or gray-box solvers, yet computing accurate data-driven models remains challenging when the dynamics exhibit large-amplitude transient energy growth. This is because state-of-the-art non-intrusive methods typically rely on orthogonal projection onto high-energy linear or nonlinear manifolds identified by minimizing static reconstruction losses, which truncates low-energy, yet dynamically important, states. Intrusive methods such as Balanced Truncation and its extensions address this issue by using adjoint information to define dynamics-aware oblique projections. Here, we show that balancing-based oblique projections for nonlinear systems can instead be computed non-intrusively from forward simulation data. Specifically, we develop a framework to compute the nonlinear empirical reachability Gramian and balance it against its observability counterpart, projected onto a suitable restriction subspace. This procedure provably recovers the oblique projection of Balanced Truncation when the dynamics are linear and the range of either Gramian is contained in the restriction subspace. Moreover, in the linear case and in the absence of adjoint information, we show that the minimax-optimal restriction subspace spans the dominant eigenspaces of the reachability Gramian, which informs an efficient balancing algorithm with cost comparable to a standard SVD. Once the oblique projection is computed, we use Operator Inference to learn the latent-space dynamics on its range. The method is demonstrated on several examples of increasing complexity, including the three-dimensional incompressible flow past a wing with $8\times 10^7$ degrees of freedom. In all examples, the Balanced Operator Inference models significantly outperform their POD-based counterparts, reducing forecasting error by up to two orders of magnitude.

papers.title: Monogamy of quantum steering in exciton--cavity optomechanical system
papers.abstract: In this work, we study a theoretical scheme to investigate the monogamy of quantum steering in a hybrid exciton--cavity optomechanical (EOM) system. Within the Gaussian-state formalism, we quantify the steerability among the exciton, photon, and mechanical modes in both the steady-state and dynamical regimes. We establish and verify CKW-type monogamy inequalities for Gaussian steering and demonstrate that the distribution of bipartite steering among the three modes can be controlled through the system parameters. We further examine the influence of thermal noise and temporal evolution on the steering properties and the corresponding monogamy relations. Our results show that increasing the temperature generally suppresses the strength of Gaussian steering and modifies the degree of steering sharing imposed by the CKW-type monogamy relations. In contrast, in the dynamical regime, the steerability can increase with evolution time over suitable temporal windows, indicating that the transient dynamics can be exploited to enhance quantum correlations. These results highlight the potential of hybrid exciton--optomechanical platforms for controllable quantum correlations and provide a promising route toward the generation and manipulation of multipartite quantum resources.
authors: Hamza Harraf, Mohamed Amazioug, Rachid Ahl Laamara

papers.title: Primordial Graviton Entanglement in Quasicrystalline Inflation
papers.abstract: We study the entanglement structure of gravitons in quasicrystalline inflation. Both parity-even and parity-odd interactions generate graviton pairs with nonzero total momentum. For opposite-helicity pairs with identical momenta, the parity-even contribution can be nonzero, whereas the parity-odd contribution vanishes. The transition from inflation to radiation domination produces additional conventional two-mode squeezing. We derive the resulting normal and anomalous covariances. The initially nonzero reciprocal blocks of the full field-momentum covariance remain nonzero under homogeneous evolution, although individual components can vanish. We show that this homogeneous, helicity-preserving evolution acts unitarily within each helicity sector and therefore preserves the entanglement between the complete right- and left-helicity sectors. Nevertheless, it can eliminate entanglement in the reduced state of a co-propagating pair. We illustrate this distinction using a solvable four-mode model.

papers.title: Valley-resolved high harmonics probe symmetry breaking beyond the Dirac cone
papers.abstract: Low-energy electrons in graphene obey an emergent, rotationally invariant Dirac equation, while the honeycomb lattice enters only through higher-order, symmetry-breaking corrections, the leading one being trigonal warping. This provides a unique solid-state arena to address a cornerstone challenge in quantum gravity: how to detect ultraviolet symmetry-breaking granular corrections, suppressed by a fundamental scale, atop an emergent infrared relativistic continuum. We show that intense counter-rotating $\omega$-$2\omega$ fields and valley-resolved high-harmonic generation (HHG) provide such a probe. Within a family of models that interpolates continuously between the isotropic Dirac cone and nearest-neighbour graphene at fixed Fermi velocity, the valley contrast of the harmonic yield vanishes identically in the symmetric theory, grows linearly with the warping coupling, and its valley-even counterpart appears only at second order, as expected from effective-field-theory power counting. The stronger the laser, the farther it drives electrons from the Dirac points, so the laser intensity plays the role of the collision energy. For the fourth harmonic, the leading warping correction alone accounts for the valley contrast of real graphene up to fundamental intensities of about $10^{11}$ W/cm$^2$, below the damage threshold of monolayer graphene, whereas the fifth harmonic already reveals higher-order lattice corrections at intensities around $10^{10}$ W/cm$^2$. The two harmonics, which rotate in opposite directions, are emitted by opposite valleys. Valley-resolved harmonics are far more sensitive than the residual valley populations, making them a practical detector of lattice-scale physics hidden beneath an emergent Dirac theory.
authors: Pablo Pais, Alfredo Iorio, Marcelo F. Ciappina

papers.title: Rydberg Atomic Quantum Receivers for OFDM Systems: An Atomic-Comb Design
papers.abstract: Rydberg atomic quantum receivers (RAQR) exhibit exceptional sensitivity to radio-frequency (RF) signals, positioning them as promising candidates for next-generation wireless systems. Extending their capabilities to orthogonal frequency-division multiplexing (OFDM), however, requires atomic responses that go beyond broadband reception and are tailored to the structured interference of multicarrier signals. To bridge this gap, we develop an atomic-comb Rydberg receiver based on six-wave mixing (SWM) transduction. In particular, injecting a multi-tone local oscillator (LO) into the RAQR generates frequency-shifted replicas of the intrinsic SWM response. By subtly tuning the amplitude and phase of each LO tone, constructive and destructive interference can be selectively induced to preserve desired response components while attenuating harmful frequency offsets. Furthermore, we harness the response-reshaping capability of the proposed atomic comb to proactively mitigate OFDM interference. More explicitly, by exploiting the discrete difference-frequency structure of both carrier-frequency-offset (CFO)-induced and phase-noise (PN)-induced inter-carrier interference (ICI), we optimize the atomic-comb response to suppress dominant ICI components directly. We further reveal an intrinsic coupling between spectral shaping and the time-domain effective channel memory, motivating a joint optimization of both ICI and inter-symbol interference (ISI), which simultaneously suppresses inter-carrier leakage and post-cyclic-prefix (CP) tail energy. Extensive simulation results validate our atomic-comb design, unveiling that the proposed atomic comb can effectively reshape the receiver response over the OFDM, while mitigating ICI, shortening the effective channel memory, and substantially lowering CP overhead.
authors: Yuanbin Chen, Chong Meng Samson See, Chau Yuen

papers.title: Photonic realization of an electromagnetic cavity field with uniform mirror motion
papers.abstract: We perform a detailed mathematical study of the effective Hamiltonian describing a non-stationary electromagnetic cavity field, introduced by C.~K.~Law, in the presence of uniform linear motion. We find that the corresponding dynamical equations admit a unitary diagonalization and that the normalized velocity of motion satisfies the two-sided bound $\lvert v/c \rvert \lesssim 10.1716$. Although this result is mathematically consistent, the interval obtained is an order of magnitude larger than the physically admissible range $\lvert v/c \rvert < 1$. To address this limitation, we propose a reinterpretation of bosonic coupling terms as generators of the symplectic algebra $\mathrm{Sp}(4,\mathbb{R})$, identifying them with transformations that can be implemented through linear optical elements. Within this photonic approach, the coupling parameters are not restricted to small values, allowing us to explore regimes of strong effective interactions. In this case, we demonstrate the generation of two-mode squeezed states and derive analytical expressions for the average photon number in each mode. Furthermore, we analyze statistical properties that characterize mixedness and entanglement, including intermode correlations, the Mandel parameter, and the linear entropy. The corresponding Wigner function provides a phase-space visualization of the system's behavior, illustrating the connection between cavity motion, mode coupling, and nonclassical field correlations via the underlying symplectic algebra.
authors: A. R. Urz\'ua, I. Ramos-Prieto, R. Rom\'an-Ancheyta, J. R\'ecamier-Angelini, L. Medina-Dozal, F. Soto-Eguibar, H. M. Moya-Cessa

papers.title: Receiver-Constrained Recovery Placement for Encoded-Qutrit Teleportation under Monitored Decay
papers.abstract: Using established probabilistic measurement-reversal theory, we study recovery placement in encoded-qutrit teleportation under monitored decay. We characterize the success advantage of reversing a no-jump map only on the encoded support and compare two receiver capabilities. The restricted-map construction applies to general finite-dimensional supports; explicit timing results are obtained for a coherent V-type sender, a $\Lambda$-type receiver, and $S=\{0,2\}$, within a prescribed family of maximal exact sender reversals. With one outcome-independent full-space receiver filter, we maximize success probability at fixed total time subject to a minimum success-weighted conditional fidelity. A single preassigned recovery time yields up to three duration-dependent regimes: no sender reversal, the earliest feasible intermediate reversal, and final-time reversal. If recovery times may be randomized independently of the input and only the pooled successful ensemble must meet the fidelity requirement, the optimum over all such timing distributions mixes the two endpoints for $\Gamma T \ge (\ln 3)/2$. With Bell-outcome-dependent nonunitary receiver recovery, each accepted full-column-rank transfer branch can instead be reversed exactly. For the same model and sender-operation family, omitting sender reversal uniquely maximizes the exact-teleportation success probability for every finite $T>0$ at positive decay rate. Partial pathway coherence further distinguishes relative support gain from absolute recovery success: the long-time dark-state plateau survives only for fully coherent decay. These results show how receiver control capabilities and the meaning of the fidelity constraint determine whether intermediate sender recovery is useful.
authors: Yifan Shi, Duan Wang, Quanzhen Ding, He Zhang, Da-Wei Luo, Ting Yu

papers.title: Type $B$- and $C$- trigonometric weight functions
papers.abstract: We introduce and study trigonometric weight functions of type $B$ and type $C$ arising from integrable lattice models. These functions give $q$-deformations of the factorial $K$-theoretic Schur $P$- and $Q$-functions of Ikeda and Naruse, with the $P$-functions specialized to the type $B$ case. We realize them as specializations of partition functions of a six-vertex model with triangular boundary conditions and derive their algebraic properties using the Yang-Baxter equation and properties of the $R$- and $K$-matrices. We introduce normalized weight functions and establish diagonal evaluation formulas, divisibility properties, and bounds on Newton polytopes analogous to those in type $A$, together with recursive relations and stability. We further derive branching formulas relating these functions to type $A$ weight functions, and prove equal-cardinality orthogonality and all-cardinality biorthogonality relations.

papers.title: Holographic theory of non-invertible gravitational anomalies
papers.abstract: We review a many-body formulation of gravitational anomalies as obstructions to realizing the complete low-energy data by a local {\it bosonic} lattice quantum system of the same dimension. In this formulation, an anomalous theory can be realized at the boundary of a gapped {\it bosonic} lattice bulk, whose topological order gives a one-to-one classification of the anomaly. An invertible bulk reproduces conventional anomaly inflow; a bulk with non-trivial topological excitations yields a non-invertible generalization. To describe the holographic theory of anomalies, we explain the distinction between uniquely defined topological order and many versions of topological quantum field theory and discuss the boundary-to-bulk map. As an application of the holographic theory of anomalies, we describe morphisms between local quantum theories (such as quantum field theories). These morphisms are built from a bulk domain wall and an invertible boundary junction, which give rise to a sandwich picture. Chiral boson/fermion theory, Laughlin edges, and boundaries of $\mathbb{Z}_2$ higher gauge theory with bosonic or fermionic point-like excitations illustrate the different kinds of information about non-invertible anomalies contained in transport coefficients, superselection sectors, and condensation data. In particular, a fermionic theory can be viewed as a theory with a particular non-invertible gravitational anomaly. Those examples also reveal that {\it symmetry $\sim$ gravitational anomaly $\sim$ topological order in one higher dimension}.

papers.title: Rank polarization and dynamical autonomy in a projective rotor model
papers.abstract: We study how a higher-rank classical collective order parameter can select one dominant projective eigenline and, in a $p=2$ realization, support a dynamically autonomous low-energy director sector. In a fully connected projective-rotor model, the collective second moment is a positive semidefinite tensor $T$ of fixed trace. Conventional projective ordering drives its effective rank toward one, selecting a single dominant eigenline. Rank polarization alone, however, does not determine dynamical autonomy: extrinsic-curvature criteria depend on the chosen state-space metric, and the equilibrium tensor does not determine the transverse free-energy Hessian. A two-harmonic model makes this logical independence explicit by producing families with identical $T$ and $r_{\rm eff}$ but different transverse quadratic forms. We then construct rotationally invariant locking interactions that leave a prescribed ordered tensor exactly fixed while increasing every non-Goldstone restoring coefficient as $\Theta(\lambda)$ within a globally controlled stable regime. For a phenomenological inertial realization with a finite positive kinetic matrix, the lowest transverse normal-mode frequency grows as $\Theta(\lambda^{1/2})$; more generally, the low-frequency transverse susceptibility is suppressed as $O(\lambda^{-1})$, including in overdamped dynamics. The construction therefore proves that spectral selection and infrared transverse suppression are independent data. For $p>2$ the selected eigenline has a $(p-1)$-dimensional director manifold; the one-dimensional Goldstone sector used in the dynamical construction is specific to $p=2$. Promoting the selected internal eigenline to a physical clock requires additional soldering and integrability structure.

papers.title: Criticality Concentrates Extensive Sensing Information into a Local Readout
papers.abstract: We show that criticality concentrates extensive sensing information into a local trajectory. In the rapid-readout limit of an all-to-all dissipative feedback network, a single binary trajectory has a Fisher-information rate linear in $N$ for a common weak field, as does the full record. Critical slowing does not remove this gain because the local weight of the slow mode decreases with $N$. An analytic bound guarantees that the local record retains more than half of the full information across the entire channel-parameter range. We also identify how parameter drives and observation dynamics determine local access to collective information beyond permutation symmetry. Furthermore, our sparse-readout theorem establishes a $k^{-1}$ decay of fractional information loss: only $\Theta(\varepsilon^{-1})$ trajectories are needed to retain a fraction $1-\varepsilon$ of the full information rate. Any growing readout set, even of vanishing density, asymptotically recovers the full common-field Fisher-information rate.
authors: Peng Wang, Yu-Xuan Zhang, Hai-Tao Ding, Leong-Chuan Kwek

papers.title: Numerical Modeling of a Metallic Alloy Droplet Impact, Solidification, and Macrosegregation
papers.abstract: For the first time, we study the effects of mass transfer on alloy droplet impact, solidification, and solute non-homogeneity or MacroSegregation (MS). For this purpose, a multi-physics model, including fully-coupled hydrodynamics of multiphase flow, wetting, conjugate heat transfer, phase change, and mass transfer, is established and validated carefully across several benchmarks. In addition, a concentration-flux-correction algorithm is proposed to conserve the solute mass within the droplet at the numerical discretization level. The validated model is subsequently used to explore the impact and solidification of an alloy droplet. The results show that accounting for mass transfer and solute transport improves the prediction of the dynamics of a solidifying splat, in a consistent manner with experimental observations, while this effect has been neglected in all previous studies. The analysis demonstrates that this improvement results from the flow sensitivity to the mushy region thickness, which is regulated by local solute concentration through the solidus and liquidus temperatures. Furthermore, analyses of the MS map identify several critical segregation regions most susceptible to defect initiation, such as cracking, including a long negatively segregated vein within the lamella, formed by the severe advective flow through the mush in the middle stages of the impact, a positively segregated region near the rim of the splat, appearing as a result of hook formation, and a major positively segregated zone at the top of the rim, which develops following the accumulation of the solute-rich melt sustained by washout from the lamella.

papers.title: Spectral geometry of saturated Fell bundles
papers.abstract: Let $\mathcal B=(B_g)_{g\in G}$ be a saturated Fell bundle over a countable discrete group, equipped with a spectral triple. We give explicit sufficient conditions for lifting this triple to the reduced cross-sectional C\Star-algebra $C_r^*(\mathcal B)$. Using finite projective realizations of the homogeneous Morita equivalence $B_e$-bimodules, we transport the base Dirac operator to the individual fibres and assemble the resulting operators into a fibrewise Dirac operator. We introduce a spectral-regularity condition ensuring bounded commutators and give a sufficient criterion in terms of uniform derivative bounds on smooth factor-system data. Combining the fibrewise operator with a length operator associated with a proper translation-bounded matrix-valued length function yields the lifted spectral triple. When $B_e$ is separable, the lifted triple, with a suitable grading, represents the Kasparov product of the vertical class with the class of the unit-fibre triple. We also establish a summability criterion and sufficient conditions for stability under central cocycle twisting. A range of examples illustrates the scope of the construction, including twisted crossed products, free compact Abelian actions, and Fell bundles with nonfree homogeneous fibres.

papers.title: Genuine Information Backflow Requires Noncommuting Initial System States
papers.abstract: The Gorini-Kossakowski-Lindblad-Sudarshan (GKLS) equation, a cornerstone of open-system theory, describes Markovian semigroup dynamics in which information about the initial preparation cannot revive. Beyond this regime, information revivals are widely interpreted as backflow from a non-Markovian environment. However, a decrease followed by an increase in information retrievable from the system need not imply that information has returned from the environment [PRX Quantum 6, 020316 (2025)]. It may instead arise from noise correlations unrelated to the system's initial preparation, carried by inert degrees of freedom that never interact with the system and therefore cannot mediate backflow. Such revivals are called extrinsic; genuine backflow is reserved for revivals that cannot be explained this way. The framework developed in that work, however, assumes access to arbitrary initial system states, an assumption often incompatible with physical constraints or limited experimental control. This leaves open which properties of the available preparations are necessary for an information revival to certify genuine backflow. Here we extend the framework to allow the description of restricted families of initial states and show that genuine backflow is possible only if the family contains noncommuting states. If all available states commute, as in a classical stochastic process, every revival can be explained by a suitable inert extension and is therefore extrinsic. Noncommutativity of the available system states is thus necessary for information revivals to provide an operational signature of environmental memory.

papers.title: Extended-range percolation on lattices with cubic and non-compact neighborhoods in three dimensions
papers.abstract: Using MC simulations based on an efficient single-cluster growth algorithm, we investigate two types of three-dimensional extended-range percolation models, namely cubic and complex (non-compact) neighborhoods. We obtain high-precision percolation thresholds $p_c$ for approximately 100 distinct structures and further explore the relationship between these thresholds and the topology of the lattices, which includes the total coordination number $z$, the number of sites $z_i$ and these sites' distance to the central site $r_i$ of the given neighborhood in the $i$th coordination zone. Both bond and site percolation are analyzed for cubic neighborhoods on the SC lattice. For bond percolation, the asymptotic value of $zp_c$ tends to Bethe-lattice behavior ($zp_c\sim1$), and finite-$z$ correction is found to be consistent with $zp_{c}-1\sim a_{1}z^{-x}$, where $x=(d-1)/d$. For site percolation, the value of $zp_c$ varies non-monotonically, exhibiting an initial increase followed by a decrease with the coordination number $z$. Linear fitting leads to $zp_c\sim2.5987(1)$ for large $z$, predicting a value of continuum percolation threshold of aligned cubes $\eta_c=0.324838(12)$ using $zp_c=2^{d}\eta_c$. We then examine site percolation for non-compact neighborhoods extending to the fifth coordination zone on SC, FCC, and BCC lattices. Through a comparison of the three indices of $z$, $\xi=\sum_iz_ir_i^2/i$, and $\zeta=\sum_iz_ir_i$, we find that $\zeta$ is effective in removing the degeneracy. The results obtained show power-law dependence $p_c\propto(\zeta/K)^{-\gamma}$ with $\gamma_{\mathrm{SC}}^{\zeta}=0.703(12)$, $\gamma_{\mathrm{FCC}}^{\zeta}=0.728(10)$, and $\gamma_{\mathrm{BCC}}^{\zeta}=0.699(12)$ for SC, FCC, and BCC lattices, and $p_c\propto\zeta^{-\gamma}$ with $\gamma^{\zeta}=0.719(9)$ independent of the underlying lattice. The number $K$ indicates lattice connectivity.
authors: Zhe Zhang, Yuxuan Fan, Yang Yang, Yusong Tu, Zhipeng Xun

papers.title: Phase transitions and quasinormal modes of Euler-Heisenberg-dilaton AdS black holes
papers.abstract: In this paper, we study phase transitions and scalar quasinormal modes(QNMs) of magnetically charged Euler--Heisenberg-dilaton AdS black holes in the extended phase space. We classify the horizon structures for all three signs of the EH coupling and derive the extended first law when the pressure and coupling are varied. For negative coupling, the physical branch exhibits a Van der Waals-like small/large black-hole transition. Using the improved asymptotic iteration method, we find two separated QNM trajectories below the critical pressure, whereas they merge into one continuous curve at the critical point. The GHS limit and the positive couplings considered here do not produce a finite-radius critical point.
authors: Yi-Qi Chen, De-Cheng Zou, Ming Zhang, Xufen Zhang, Bo Liu, Rui-Hong Yue

papers.title: Quantum circuit representation and incomplete Bell measurements in Compton scattering
papers.abstract: We formulate massless tree-level Compton scattering as an effective two-qubit operation on electron and photon helicities. In the Bell basis, the scattering map separates into two parity sectors and admits a simple quantum circuit representation with one nonunitary filter. After Kraus normalization, this filter defines an unsharp incomplete Bell measurement that distinguishes the two Bell-parity sectors but not the relative Bell label within each sector. We further show that the incomplete measurement alone does not surpass the classical teleportation threshold, whereas a subsequent complete Bell-basis readout enables unit conditional teleportation fidelity.
authors: Wei Xie, Yu-Chen Guo, Shuang Li, Ji-Chong Yang

papers.title: Breakdown of thermalization in quantum spin systems with long-range interactions
papers.abstract: Quantum thermalization of closed systems -- i.e. the relaxation of local properties to their thermodynamic value along the Hamiltonian evolution -- is generically expected in non-integrable systems at finite energy density. In this work we show that quantum spin systems with at least one spin component coupled through long-range ferromagnetic interactions, and a second spin component coupled to a field, cannot in general thermalize to a paramagnetic state whenever they have a finite, negative energy per spin. The long-range interactions we consider decay as a power law of the distance, $\sim r^{-\alpha}$ with $\alpha < d$, where $d$ is the number of spatial dimensions of the system. The lack of thermalization is generic to an infinite family of Hamiltonians, and it is not associated to any form of integrability. It can instead be understood by the anomalous features of the thermodynamics of the system in the paramagnetic phase, which cannot be reflected in the properties of the eigenstates. This leads to a breakdown of eigenstate typicality and of the eigenstate thermalization hypothesis. Interestingly, the non-thermal states emerging at long times in the dynamics display long-range multipartite entanglement, elevating the breakdown of thermalization to a resource.
authors: Filippo Caleca, Fabio Mezzacapo, Tommaso Roscilde

papers.title: Generalized Constraint-Controlled Rheological Model: Two Constitutive Pathways under Sinusoidal Periodic Shear Deformation
papers.abstract: We formulate the Generalized Constraint-Controlled Rheological Model (GCCRM) for entangled linear and long-arm-branched polymer melts under sinusoidal periodic shear deformation (SPSD), spanning the linear and strongly nonlinear regimes. Molecular architecture, conformation, chain stretch, flow-active constraints, convective constraint release, dynamic tube dilation, and activated arm retraction define a common upstream molecular state. This state feeds two time-domain constitutive pathways (a configurational stress and a dissipative internal-variable stress) which are recombined before Fourier analysis. For branched polymers, the architecture is described by an entire backbone of molecular weight $M_{bb}$ and $N_a$ long arms of molecular weight $M_a$, with a compliance-weighted representative-constitutive-cell partition. The linear limit is normalized so that the configurational moduli sum to the entanglement modulus, while dynamic tube dilation and stretch drive distinct contributions to dissipative activation. Under reduced closures, GCCRM generates a smooth nonlinear elastic response with an onset of nonlinearity, an approximately logarithmic growth regime, an architecture-dependent maximum, and distinct high-deformation asymptotes. Fourier harmonics, ELR, VLR, and Lissajous curves are treated as post-processing observables of the total stress. The framework establishes a consistent constitutive architecture whose quantitative validation requires one parameter set per material across SPSD and, prospectively, transient shear histories.

papers.title: Ergodicity breaking transition beyond qubits
papers.abstract: The local Hilbert space dimension is a fundamental parameter in quantum many-body systems, but its role in controlling the ergodicity-breaking transition remains less explored. We systematically study this question by introducing toy models of qudits in zero dimensions that exhibit an ergodicity-breaking transition. Using the hybridization condition, we analytically obtain the dependence of the critical value of the interactions on the local Hilbert space dimension. Numerical studies of spectral correlation measures show agreement with the theoretical predictions, hence confirming the existence of the ergodicity-breaking transition in these models. We further introduce a distinct higher spin version of the model and numerically obtain the same critical behavior, demonstrating that the observed critical point is independent of the microscopic structure of interactions considered.

papers.title: Modular $S_4$ Inverse Seesaw at the LZ High-Recoil Frontier
papers.abstract: The extension of the LUX--ZEPLIN nuclear-recoil analysis to approximately $270\,\mathrm{keV}$ probes a qualitatively new dark-matter regime in which endothermic scattering can suppress conventional low-energy recoils and concentrate the surviving spectrum near the Galactic high-velocity tail. We construct a modular-$S_4$ realization in which a minimal $2N_R+2S$ inverse seesaw accounts for lepton flavor, while a separate pair of Standard-Model-singlet fermions forms the pseudo-Dirac state relevant for high-recoil xenon scattering. The sectors share a common complex modulus $\tau$, so the modular forms selected by charged-lepton and neutrino data also enter the operators generating the dark Dirac mass and Majorana splitting. Our scan yields $181447$ lepton-sector solutions satisfying $\chi^2_{\ell+\nu}<30$, distributed among several disconnected modular regions, and predicts one effectively massless light neutrino at leading order. Restoring the physical scales allows TeV-scale heavy quasi-Dirac neutral fermions with small non-unitarity. We subsequently scan $2\times10^6$ dark-sector points only over flavor-accepted values of $\tau$ and identify common-modulus solutions in the LZ-oriented region $300\,\mathrm{GeV}\le m_\chi\le2\,\mathrm{TeV}$ and $300\,\mathrm{keV}\le\delta\le400\,\mathrm{keV}$. An exploratory two-bin Poisson likelihood, including endothermic xenon kinematics, the Helm form factor, Standard-Halo-Model velocities, Gaussian energy smearing, and profiling over the signal normalization, gives a best grid point at $(m_\chi,\delta)\simeq(1.847\,\mathrm{TeV},371.5\,\mathrm{keV})$, close to the terrestrial inelastic kinematic ceiling. The construction provides a direct link between modular lepton flavor, TeV-scale inverse-seesaw dynamics, and high-recoil inelastic dark matter.
authors: Waqas Ahmed, Vasileios Basiouris, George K. Leontaris

papers.title: Dynamical chiral symmetry breaking in rotating QED$_3$: critical flavor number and the occupation-reweighting channel
papers.abstract: We study dynamical chiral symmetry breaking in $(2{+}1)$-dimensional QED on a rigidly rotating disc, $\Omega R<1$, within the rainbow Schwinger--Dyson framework. At zero temperature the rotation response of the condensate vanishes identically, so $N_c^{\rm SD}(\Omega,T{=}0)=N_c^{\rm SD}(0)=2.60\pm0.01$ (using three operational definitions). At finite temperature, rotation suppresses the condensate through a dominant occupation-reweighting channel, $\hat{\kappa}_{\rm occ}=-1.55$, accounting for $\ge 99.995\%$ of the linearized total response at the reference parameters, with self-consistent feedback amplifying it by $26.5$. The screening channel is reported at fixed regularization, $\hat{\kappa}_{\rm scr}(\varepsilon = 0.01)=-0.97$; its $\varepsilon \to 0$ behavior is logarithmically divergent. The crossover flavor $N^{*}(\Omega)$ falls monotonically at fixed temperature (a corollary). The critical flavor number is unchanged by rotation at $T=0$ (theorem). Together these results set the finite-temperature reference for the model.

papers.title: Riemannian Formulation of Sample-Based Quantum Krylov Solvers for Elliptic Problems: Energy-Norm Guarantees and Duct-Flow Applications
papers.abstract: Sample-based quantum linear solvers measure quantum Krylov states $e^{-iAT}|b\rangle$ and reconstruct the solution of $Ax=b$ classically on the observed basis states. We develop this approach for positive-definite systems that arise from elliptic partial differential equations. We show that the sampling guarantees hold in any fixed basis with an efficient transform. We then replace the variational reconstruction by a Galerkin solve on the sampled set. For this reconstruction we derive expected and high-probability energy-norm error bounds, a sample complexity in terms of the smallest sampling probability on an essential set, a computable residual certificate, and a support-completeness theorem for the dephased outcome law. We formulate the method for elliptic problems on Riemannian cross sections. In two dimensions the stiffness matrix is metric-independent in conformal coordinates, and curved vessels lead to the same matrix class. Killing symmetries of the cross section give selection rules for the measurement outcomes, and the Lie derivative of the metric gives first-order bounds for geometric perturbations. We separate operator approximations, whose effect we bound, from sampler approximations, which affect coverage but not the target. As examples we treat the implicit step of pulsatile flow in elliptic, lens-shaped, and curved ducts. In simulations of up to 12 qubits, the number of Fourier modes required for 1% error grows from 14 to 60 while the number of unknowns grows from 64 to 4096. A classical residual-greedy selection is nevertheless more efficient than quantum sampling in all cases studied, consistent with the low measured sampling efficiency. On a six-qubit trapped-ion processor, the measured outcome laws follow a replacement-noise model whose strength grows by about 0.6% per two-qubit gate, and a parity selection rule rejects shots at the predicted rate.
authors: Doyeol "David" Ahn (Center for Quantum Information Processing, University of Seoul, Dongdaemun-gu, Seoul, Republic of Korea, Singularity Quantum Inc., Villa Park, California, USA), Byeongyong Park (Center for Quantum Information Processing, University of Seoul, Dongdaemun-gu, Seoul, Republic of Korea)

papers.title: A Quantum Analogue of the Covering Lemma: Limits of Exact Anonymous Computation
papers.abstract: Can quantum communication determine the size of an anonymous network when no size bound is known? Classical impossibility proofs rely on the covering lemma: an execution can be reproduced on a larger network with the same local structure. Quantum interference invalidates this argument - a measurement record possible on a network can become impossible on a cover. We show that the impossibility of exact counting nevertheless survives. Our main result is a quantum analogue of the covering lemma that preserves local possibilities rather than complete executions. Within a cyclic covering family, every local measurement outcome possible at a node remains possible at a corresponding node in every sufficiently large network. This holds even after information has travelled around the smaller network, beyond the reach of a simple locality argument. We extend the principle to the universal covering tree and finite covers with sufficiently long cycles. The proof combines tensor-network methods with graph coverings: a common representation across network sizes turns normalization into a constraint on which local outcomes can occur. For uniform synchronous protocols with independently prepared nodes, this support-lifting principle rules out zero-error counting and even the production of a guaranteed finite size bound on anonymous rings and the other cyclic covering families considered here. It also rules out exact leader election with termination in finite time with probability one on these families.
